page: OVHcloud c3-64 is a compute-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, with a thread-per-core ratio of 1.0, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 98610.77 and single-core score of 3083.01 both rank in the top 25%. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with a Passmark memory score of 2995.4 placing it in the top 10%, supported by a read-only small block cached memory bandwidth of 4755.88 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 433.64 GB/sec, also in the top 25%. However, single-threaded gzip compression at 29.15 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 31.07 GB/sec perform in the middle 50% average tier.

This server is configured for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading overhead, such as parallel processing, database operations, and small-scale machine learning inference. The Passmark database operations score of 31841.07 and Redis SET throughput of 77.38 million operations per second demonstrate strong database capabilities. For AI workloads, the system processes prompts at 2858.15 tokens per second on a small 135M model, though performance drops to an average tier of 152.91 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints.
